resources.string: Status and navigation bars are hidden. Swipe from an edge to reveal them.
Status and navigation bars stay visible; content is kept clear of them.
Scales the whole terminal UI — pills included — not just the text. Between 85 and 200 percent.

Runs commands over the app’s own native pty bridge instead of a plain pipe, so full-screen tools (vim, top, less, an interactive REPL) can draw a screen instead of breaking. On by default; switch to PIPE only if a tool misbehaves. Takes effect for a new tab or the next app launch, not the one you’re in.
The interactive shell used for new HG2Gui sessions. Only installed shells are shown. Changing it does not replace the shell in an already-running tab.
No installed shell was found, so there is nothing to choose here.
The PATH and env vars every command actually runs under - the same map ShellSession builds fresh for each bootstrap-tier session. Read-only.
Every command run in any tab, searchable - not just the current tab’s own up/down-arrow recall.
Inspect the latest observed process, file, network, and authority activity from packages running inside HG2Gui isolation.
The API key AI command search/chat uses to suggest shell commands. Off until a key is set.
A loopback-only MCP server a paired AI agent can connect to, and the biometric-gated switch that lets it run real shell commands.
HG2Gui checks GitHub for a newer build when it starts (at most every six hours) and posts a notification if there is one. Tapping the notification downloads and installs it.
Off. HG2Gui never contacts GitHub on its own to look for updates.
HG2Gui follows Android’s animation setting, and animations are on. To turn them off, use Remove animations in Android’s accessibility settings (or the Animator duration scale in developer options).
Animations are off in Android’s settings, so HG2Gui skips its entrance and transition effects and shows screens straight away.

An Anthropic API key, used only for the AI command-search chat and for Isolation audit’s Ask AI, which sends a summary of that package’s sandbox changes and observed activity to Anthropic when you tap it. Stored encrypted on this device (Android Keystore).
Error: the key could not be saved. This device’s secure storage is unavailable, so the key would be lost when HG2Gui closes. Try again, or restart the app.
Your edit to the API key has not been saved. Leaving now discards it.
Running on 127.0.0.1:%1$s, reachable by any app on this device (not just over the network) — the token below is what actually gates it. Present it once to pair.
Off. Starting it opens a loopback socket any app on this device can connect to (not just via adb forward) to read/write this app’s sandboxed files, gated by a pairing token.

Error: the server did not start because HG2Gui is not allowed to post notifications. That notification is the only visible sign that the server is running, so it stays off until notifications are allowed.
Required on every connection. Regenerated fresh each time the server starts — never shown to anyone but you.
Copy the pairing token to the clipboard
Pairing token copied to the clipboard.
Run this on the computer connected over USB to forward the port, then point the agent at 127.0.0.1 with the pairing token.
Copy the adb forward command to the clipboard
The adb forward command was copied to the clipboard.
Enabled — a paired agent can run real shell commands, on a session separate from your own terminal tabs. Confirmed by biometric unlock.
Disabled by default. Enabling it requires a biometric confirmation — this is the one switch in this screen that lets a connected agent run arbitrary commands, not just read/write sandboxed files.
Add an Anthropic API key in Settings → AI first.
Describe what you want to do and the AI suggests a shell command. Nothing runs until you have reviewed it and pressed RUN.

%1$s by %2$s is a skill: its text is added to the AI chat’s instructions and can steer the commands the AI suggests. Its signature can only be checked after it is downloaded, and anyone can self-sign. Install it only if you trust the author.
